# The True Cost of Buying a Manufactured Home: What to Budget for Beyond the Base Price of the Home


Published On: November 25, 2026


•


6 min read


•


The listed price of a[manufactured home](https://www.cavcohomes.com/find-a-floor-plan) is only one part of your total cost. Land, site work, utility hookups, permits, financing and insurance can each add to your budget. Some of those expenses may already be included in your[Cavco retailer](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers) 's quote, while others may be additional costs to factor in.


If you own land with utilities nearby, your additional costs may be relatively modest. Starting with undeveloped rural land can require a larger investment. We'll explain the expenses to take into consideration, what can affect them and how to build a realistic budget before buying your home.


## **What does the base price include?**


Typically, the base price only includes the cost of the home itself. However, Cavco homes are sold through local retailers from coast to coast, and each location sets its own turnkey pricing. A


**turnkey quote** often bundles the home with the services needed to move in.


Your quote may include:


- **The home:** floor plan, base price and any upgrades


- **Delivery:** transport from the factory to your site


- **Site preparation:** clearing, grading or other groundwork, if listed


- **Installation:** joining sections, leveling and anchoring


- **Utility connections:** water, sewer or septic, and electric


- **Finishing work:** steps, decks and skirting


Details vary by retailer. Ask for an itemized written quote and compare total packages, not advertised prices.

## **How much does land add?**


If you own land, you skip the biggest single expense, but the lot may not yet be ready for your manufactured home. Check these first:


- **Zoning:** whether your parcel allows for a manufactured home


- **Deed restrictions:** covenants or homeowners' association (HOA) rules that might limit placement


- **Site conditions:** slope, soil and access that can rule out certain homes


You may still need clearing, leveling, a foundation, utilities and permits. All of these would require you to budget for extra expenses beyond the price of your home.


Depending on your market, many Cavco retailers offer:


- **Search guidance:** tips on how to start your land hunt


- **Referrals:** local real estate professionals who know suitable manufactured home-ready land


- **Retailer-owned lots:** land sold with the home in some markets


- **Move-in-ready homes:** homes already placed on land

## **Don't want to buy land? Place your home in a land-lease community.**


In a land-lease community, you own the home and rent the lot, which often comes with utilities.


[MHInsider's 2026 State of the Industry](https://mhinsider.com/state-of-the-industry-2026/) report put average monthly lot rent near $780 in 2025. Before signing, ask:


- **Rent coverage:** what the monthly rent includes


- **Utilities:** whether they're billed separately


- **Increases:** how rent increases work


- **Rules:** which community standards apply

## **What does site preparation cost?**


Angi’s 2026 guide puts general residential site preparation at roughly $1,000 to $6,000, with tough properties costing more. These are broad estimates, not manufactured home quotes. Typical work includes:


- **Land clearing:** removing trees, brush, rocks and stumps


- **Grading:** leveling the ground and sloping it so water runs away from the home


- **Soil testing:** checking ground conditions to set foundation requirements


- **Drainage work:** controlling runoff to prevent erosion and moisture problems


Every home needs a support and anchoring system that follows its installation instructions and local rules, and your lender may add requirements. Fannie Mae requires a permanent foundation suited to the soil and compliant with local and state codes (Selling Guide B2-3-02). FHA requires a permanent foundation built to FHA criteria, and an engineer’s certification may be needed. A cheaper support system could limit your loan options, so your foundation choice is a financing choice. Credible national foundation prices are scarce, so get local quotes.


Delivery trucks need a path in. These can mean fixes before the home arrives:


- **Narrow driveways**


- **Steep slopes**


- **Removing low branches**


- **Overhead lines**


- **Soft ground**


Walk the route with your retailer.

## **What does it cost to connect utilities?**


On undeveloped land, utilities can be your largest expense.[Angi’s 2026 guide to vacant land](https://www.angi.com/articles/site-development-costs.htm) puts general residential utility installation at roughly $6,000 to $30,000 or more. That’s a ballpark estimate, not a hard quote. Budget for:


- **Electricity:** extending service, installing a meter and connecting the home


- **Water:** a public connection or a private well


- **Wastewater:** a public sewer connection or a septic system


If lines don’t reach your lot, expect charges for poles, trenching or underground runs. Ask each provider what its estimate covers.


Most communities require a site evaluation before a septic system goes in, often with a perc test that measures how well soil absorbs water. Angi puts perc testing at about $750 to $1,900. Poor soil can call for a costlier engineered system or even rule out the site.


## **Are delivery, installation and setup fees included?**


Many turnkey quotes include delivery and setting the home on its foundation. Confirm it. These factors can affect the price:


- **Factory distance**


- **Section count**


- **Road conditions**


- **Lot accessibility**


Skirting, steps, porches, decks and carports may sit outside the base quote.


[Find A Dealer](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers)


## **What permits and fees apply?**


Expect fees and expenses relating to any of these:


- **Site and installation permits:** approvals for groundwork, foundation and setup


- **Utility permits:** electrical, plumbing, water and sewer


- **Well and septic permits:** private water or wastewater systems


- **Inspections:** foundation, anchoring and utility work


- **Development fees:** charges for utility connections or driveway development


## **How do financing and closing costs affect the total cost?**


Financing a factory-built home looks a lot like financing an onsite-built home. Cavco's subsidiary,


[CountryPlace Mortgage](https://www.countryplaceloans.com/) , specializes in manufactured and modular loans. Three things shape your upfront cash:


- **Down payment**


- **Loan terms**


- **Closing costs:** the


[Consumer Financial Protection Bureau](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/) (CFPB) says these run 2% to 5% of the purchase price on a typical mortgage, excluding the down payment


That's a general mortgage figure, so ask your lender for an itemized estimate.


Your loan type depends on how the home is classified:


- **Real-property mortgage:** for a home permanently attached to land you own and classified as real estate. Converting the title from vehicle-style to real property is required, and the process depends on state law. Ask your lender and title company early.


- **Chattel loan:** a personal-property loan that doesn't use land as collateral, suited to leased land.


## **What about property taxes and insurance?**


- **Property taxes:** assessment rules vary by state and county. A real-property home may be assessed with the land, and a personal-property home may be assessed separately. Call your county assessor.


- **Insurance:** premiums depend on location, home age and size, coverage limits and deductibles. Request quotes for your specific home.


- **Cavco options:**[Standard Casualty Company](https://www.stdins.com/) and


[Cedarbrook Insurance Group](https://cedarbrookinsurance.com/) serve homeowners.


## **How to calculate your total**


Start with your retailer's written quote and list what it leaves out. Budget these five upfront categories:


- **Home and land:** the home, upgrades and any land purchase amount


- **Site preparation and utilities:** clearing, grading, foundation, driveway, water, electric and wastewater


- **Delivery and installation:** transport, setup and finishing work not in the quote


- **Permits and financing:** approvals, inspections, down payment and closing costs


- **Extras:** insurance, moving costs and a cushion for surprises


Keep a separate monthly budget for loan payments, property taxes, insurance, utilities, maintenance and lot rent.
